messages:
maria (infra): seeing a weird cascade on eu-west NVMe nodes — janitor cleanup + smallwrite churn turned into an I/O snowball, blocking gpu attach for several pools. ops-bot: alert: /alerts/ephemeral-iops-spike triggered on eu-west2 (avg iops x5 baseline). maria (infra): timeline: at ~03:10 janitor started aggressive sweep, by 03:14 iops climbed, 03:16 attach failures for gpu-provisioner. leo (sre): seen error in attach logs: "device busy: nvme queue depth exhausted". can someone paste recent scrub config? ashwin (eng-infra): scrub cadence was lowered in last deploy (PR #4532) — aggressive window set to 5m for tempdir cleanup to reduce latencies during heavy batch windows. probably overshot. sophie (oncall): impact: ~12 pending gpu attaches in eu-west, 3 failed jobs retried. cost spike noted from provisioning retries. maria (infra): immediate mitigation: can we pause janitor on eu-west pools for 30m? janitor-bot: pausing janitor for label=ephemeral-eu-west2 by request of maria (infra). ashwin (eng-infra): doing soft pause now on canary nodes, pushing roll back to scrub cadence to 20m. command: `kubectl -n infra patch cronjob janitor-cleaner --patch '{"spec":{"schedule":"*/20 * * * *"}}'` leo (sre): also throttling background fsyncs on target hosts (`echo 64 > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/nr_requests`) — will need kernel safe window, doing on 3 hosts. ops-bot: grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ephemeral-iops?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west2 — showing prefix write rate spike. sophie (oncall): do we need to cordon some nodes to free nvme pressure before gpu attach? maria (infra): prefer avoid cordon if we can throttle janitor + bump attach timeout. ashwin (eng-infra): bumping attach timeout from 30s -> 90s in provisioner config now. snippet: ```yaml
provisioner:
  attachTimeoutSeconds: 90
``` leo (sre): quick check: smartctl shows no SMART failures, wear % steady — this is load pattern, not hardware. maria (infra): yes, not hardware. root cause: cleanup scheduling + many tiny file deletions -> metadata write storm -> NVMe queue depth exhaustion -> gpu attach fails. ashwin (eng-infra): long-term idea: make janitor size-aware and exponential backoff when observed iops > threshold. also add KV prefix caching for tempfile deletions. sophie (oncall): alerting tweak: add composite alert rule so scrub spike correlates with attach-failures before paging. ops-bot: note added: runbook link /runbooks/io-snowball-ephemeral.md (draft). leo (sre): for now, status: janitor paused, attach timeout increased, throttling applied on 3 hosts, backlog clearing. monitoring: iops back to 1.4x baseline and attach queue draining. maria (infra): thanks — will keep this thread updated. ashwin (eng-infra): follow-up tasks: create canary for janitor with real iops guard, add metrics for tempfile churn, and postmortem if this repeats. sophie (oncall): tagging product/sre for cost hit visibility. maria (infra): small note: set cost flag for failing retries -> bill center infra-ops. leo (sre): leaving a quick syslog snippet in case useful: \n```
Mar 25 03:16 gnode-128 provisioner[2123]: attach failed: rpc timeout, nvme io wait high
Mar 25 03:16 gnode-128 kernel: nvme0: submission queue full, qdepth=1024
```
ashwin (eng-infra): will open follow-up ticket: INFRA-2741 (janitor rate limit + iops safety). maria (infra): closing immediate incident — reopen if iops > 2x baseline. :white_check_mark:
